label: Ubiquiti UniFi Switch 16 (US-16-150W)
description: UniFi Switch 16 PoE+ (US-16-150W) - 16x 1G RJ45 all PoE/PoE+ with 24V passive PoE on the same ports, 2x 1G SFP, serial console, 122 W PoE budget.
notes:
Vendor rows, all Ubiquiti-hosted, read 2026-11-20. Datasheet "https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/unifi/UniFi_PoE_Switch.pdf" (HTTP 200, 3,962,155 B, 12 pp, text layer; the link the product's own page serves, `https://www.ui.com/downloads/datasheets/unifi/UniFi_PoE_Switch.pdf`, 301s here). Model bullets (printed p.3): "Model: US-16-150W - (16) Gigabit RJ45 Ports - (2) SFP Ports - (1) Serial Console Port - Non-Blocking Throughput: 18 Gbps - Switching Capacity: 36 Gbps - Forwarding Rate: 26.78 Mpps - Maximum Power Consumption: 150W". Spec table (printed p.7): Networking Interfaces "(16) 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45 Ethernet Ports / (2) 1 Gbps SFP Ethernet Ports"; Management Interface "Ethernet In-Band"; Power Supply "AC/DC, Internal, 150W DC"; Max. Power Consumption "Including PoE Output 150W / Excluding PoE Output 28W"; PoE Interfaces "PoE+ IEEE 802.3af/at (Pins 1, 2+; 3, 6-); 24VDC Passive PoE (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)"; Max. PoE+ Wattage per Port by PSE "34.2W"; Max. Passive PoE Wattage per Port "17W".

The correction in this pass is the budget. This row served 150 W - the model-name figure, which is the whole-box ceiling including PoE. Ubiquiti publishes 122 W of PoE availability (see `poe.note`), so the old number handed out 28 W the supply cannot allocate. 122 W across sixteen ports is 7.6 W average, not the 9.4 W this note used to claim: enough for sixteen cameras, not for sixteen 802.3at APs, and the per-port ceiling (34.2 W PoE+ by the datasheet, 32 W by the store page) is what caps a partial fill.

Two vendor inconsistencies are recorded rather than resolved. (1) The spec table's Management Interface row reads only "Ethernet In-Band" while the model bullets on p.3 list "(1) Serial Console Port" for this SKU (US-8-150W has neither, US-24-250W and up print "(1) RJ45 Serial Port Out-of-Band, Ethernet In-Band" in the table). The console interface stays, on the bullet and on the store page's feature list. (2) Per-port PoE+ ceiling is 34.2 W in the datasheet and 32 W on the storefront, the same split the EdgeSwitch generation shows.

The two SFP cages are 1G, not SFP+; this datasheet gives the 48-port models the two 10G cages. Copper prints as 10/100/1000 on both vendor surfaces, so `10M` stays in `speedCaps`.

poe.note: Ubiquiti's own row, not a subtraction of ours: the archived store page's spec table prints "Total available PoE 122W", repeats it as the key feature "122W total PoE availability", tags the SKU `poe:122w`, and titles the shelf row "Standard 16 PoE (Gen1) US-16-150W (122W)". The same table gives "Max. power consumption: Excluding PoE output: 28W / Including PoE output: 150W" and the datasheet prints the same pair, so 150 W is the supply and whole-box ceiling while 122 W is what powered devices may draw (150 - 28 = 122). Per port by PSE the datasheet prints "PoE+ 34.2W / Max. Passive PoE 17W"; the store page prints "32W / 17W" for the same two rows. Both are recorded; neither is used as a budget. No live tech-spec page can be cited instead: `techspecs.ui.com/unifi/switching/us-16-150w` is a 307 to `/` (1 byte) and `dl.ui.com/ds/us-16-150w_ds.pdf` a 302 to the techspecs root, so the archived storefront is the vendor surface that survives.
